title: The Meter Never Came: Morgan Forecloses Tesla's Wireless Dream for Want of a Billable Model

extractionLoop.stage1_upfrontSkim: Morgan's $150,000 subscription bought a stake in a plant — Wardenclyffe, at Shoreham, Long Island — whose projected business was transatlantic wireless telegraphy with, per Tesla's plans, an eventual horizon of global power transmission.
extractionLoop.stage2_structuralCompromise: Marconi's December 1901 transatlantic signal demonstrated the wireless telegraphy Morgan had financed on far less capital and with a billable point-to-point model, collapsing Tesla's strategic position without a single transaction of Tesla's own failing.
extractionLoop.stage3_informationFog: The speculative character of Tesla's power-transmission ambitions was unpriced and unreportable in 1901 — no market existed to value it, and Morgan's decision-making about further funding left no public record contemporaneously.
extractionLoop.stage4_monopolyWindfall: Morgan's withdrawal, and the capital's flight to Marconi's patent-protected model, delivered the wireless market to a patent pool (Marconi's company, backed by British and American capital) while Tesla's tower stood unfinished until demolition in 1917.
extractionLoop.stage5_merseyWhitewash: The affair passed into finance lore as a personal story of Tesla's eccentricity rather than a structure: the record shows funding withdrawn after a competitor's success, not an audit of the un-metered technology's feasibility.

closedLoopRatchet.inheritedFramework: The episode inherited the patent-as-choke-point machinery of the electrical age — Edison's patent litigation model, the General Electric cartel framework Morgan had already financed — and applied it to the ether.
closedLoopRatchet.newFrameworkCreated: Marconi's victory established the patent-protected wireless monopoly as the template for spectrum businesses, culminating in the 1943 Supreme Court finding (Marconi Wireless Telegraph Co. v. United States, 320 U.S. 1) that Tesla's prior patents anticipated parts of Marconi's patent.
closedLoopRatchet.closedLoopRecirculation: Capital that declined Tesla's un-metered model flowed to the Marconi company's metered service and returned as patent-protected rents for its backers, while Tesla's property was mortgaged, lost, and eventually dynamited.
closedLoopRatchet.enablesNextDossier: The wireless patent war established the choke-point-on-the-spectrum model that later radio, radar, and communications dossiers document, with the state (via courts and later regulation) as the ultimate issuer of exclusivity.

decoyVsLedger.viralDecoy: The legend of Morgan asking Tesla 'where do we put the meter?' and withdrawing upon hearing that power would be free — a tale of a financier strangling a utopia for want of tolls.
decoyVsLedger.whyDecoyFails: The meter quote is not documented; the verifiable record is Morgan declining further funding after Marconi's December 1901 transatlantic signal demonstrated the service on less capital, and Tesla losing the property — no intrigue required, just a billable model beating an unbuilt one.
decoyVsLedger.documentedLedger: The documented ledger: Morgan's $150,000 commitment, the 1901 start of construction at Wardenclyffe, Marconi's December 1901 transatlantic signal, the withdrawal of further funding, the property's mortgage and loss, the 1917 demolition, and the 1943 Supreme Court opinion (320 U.S. 1) finding Tesla's prior patents anticipated parts of Marconi's — all on public record.
